title.zh: 卷五十 志第十九: 禮志二
title.raw: 卷五十 志第十九: 禮志二 Volume 50 Treatises 20: Rites 2

sentences.zh: 禮志二 ○凶儀

translations.literal: Rites Treatise, Part Two ○ Inauspicious Rites
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites II — Mourning and Funeral Rites

sentences.zh: 喪葬儀：聖宗崩，興宗哭臨於菆塗殿。

translations.literal: Funeral rites: When Emperor Shengzong died, Emperor Xingzong mourned at the bier in the Zangtu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites: When Emperor Shengzong passed away, Emperor Xingzong came to mourn at the bier in the Zangtu Hall.

sentences.zh: 大行之夕四鼓終，皇帝率群臣入，柩前三致奠，奉柩出殿之西北門，就辒京車，藉以素裀。

translations.literal: On the night of the late emperor's passing, when the fourth watch ended, the emperor led the officials in; before the bier they presented offerings three times, bore the bier out through the hall's northwest gate, placed it on the encoffining carriage, and spread a plain white mat beneath.
translations.idiomatic: On the night the late emperor died, after the fourth watch had ended, the emperor led his ministers inside. Before the bier they presented offerings three times, then carried the coffin out through the northwest gate of the hall, set it on the encoffining carriage, and laid a plain white mat underneath.

sentences.zh: 巫者袚除之。

translations.literal: Shamans performed purification upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans performed the rites of purification.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，發引，至祭，凡五致奠。

translations.literal: At dawn the procession set out; from departure to sacrifice, offerings were presented five times in all.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the funeral procession departed; from the setting out to the sacrifice, offerings were presented five times in all.

sentences.zh: 太巫祈禳。

translations.literal: The grand shaman prayed for expiation.
translations.idiomatic: The grand shaman offered prayers of expiation.

sentences.zh: 皇族、外戚、大臣、諸京官以次致祭。

translations.literal: The imperial clan, maternal kin, great ministers, and officials of the various capitals offered sacrifice in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the imperial clan, maternal relatives, great ministers, and officials from the various capitals offered sacrifice in succession.

sentences.zh: 乃以衣、弓矢、鞍勒、圖畫、馬駝、儀衛等物皆燔之。

translations.literal: Then clothing, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, paintings, horses and camels, ceremonial guards, and the like were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Then clothing, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, paintings, horses and camels, ceremonial regalia, and the like were all consigned to the flames.

sentences.zh: 至山陵，葬畢，上哀冊。

translations.literal: When they reached the imperial tomb and the burial was complete, the lamentation document was presented.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the imperial tomb and the burial was finished, the lamentation document was presented.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御幄，命改火，面火致奠，三拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sat in the imperial tent, ordered the fire to be changed, faced the fire to present offerings, and bowed three times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his seat in the imperial tent, ordered the mourning fire to be kindled anew, faced the fire to present offerings, and bowed three times.

sentences.zh: 又東向，再拜天地訖，乘馬，率送葬者過神門之木乃下，東向又再拜。

translations.literal: He then faced east and bowed twice more to Heaven and Earth; when this was done he mounted his horse, led the funeral party past the spirit-gate tree before dismounting, and bowed twice again facing east.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned eastward and bowed twice to Heaven and Earth. When this was done he mounted his horse and led the funeral party past the spirit-gate tree before dismounting and bowing twice again toward the east.

sentences.zh: 翼日詰旦，率群臣、命婦詣山陵，行初奠之禮。

translations.literal: On the morrow at dawn he led the officials and titled ladies to the imperial tomb to perform the first offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the following morning at dawn he led the officials and titled ladies to the imperial tomb to perform the first offering rite.

sentences.zh: 升御容殿，受遺賜。

translations.literal: He ascended the Hall of Imperial Portrait and received the bequeathed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the Hall of Imperial Portrait and received the late emperor's bequeathed gifts.

sentences.zh: 又翼日，再奠如初。

translations.literal: On the following day the second offering was performed as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the day after that, the second offering was performed in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 興宗崩，道宗親擇地以葬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xingzong died, Emperor Daozong personally chose the burial site.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xingzong died, Emperor Daozong personally selected the ground for his burial.

sentences.zh: 道宗崩，菆塗於遊仙殿，有司奉喪服。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daozong died, the body was laid out at the Youxian Hall; the proper offices presented mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daozong died, the body was laid out in the Youxian Hall, and the responsible offices presented the mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 天祚皇帝問禮於總知翰林院事耶律固，始服斬衰；

translations.literal: Emperor Tianzuo asked Supervisor of the Hanlin Academy Ye Lü Gu about the rites and then donned the deepest mourning of unhemmed sackcloth;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianzuo inquired about the rites from Ye Lü Gu, Supervisor of the Hanlin Academy, and then put on the deepest mourning garment of unhemmed sackcloth;

sentences.zh: 皇族、外戚、使相、矮墩官及郎君服如之；

translations.literal: the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, officials of the Aidian rank, and langjun wore the same;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, officials of Aidian rank, and langjun wore the same;

sentences.zh: 餘官及承應人皆白掞衣巾以入，哭臨。

translations.literal: all other officials and attendants entered in white mourning dress and headcloth to mourn at the bier.
translations.idiomatic: all remaining officials and attendants entered wearing white mourning dress and headcloths to mourn at the bier.

sentences.zh: 惕隱、三父房，南府宰相、遙輦常袞、九奚首郎君、夷離畢、國舅詳穩、十閘撒郎君、南院大王、郎君，各以次薦奠，進鞍馬、衣襲、犀玉帶等物，表列其數。

translations.literal: Tieli, the Three Fathers' House, the Southern Chancellor, Yaonian Changgun, the Nine Xishou Langjun, Yilibi, Guoguo Xiangwen, the Ten Zhacha Langjun, the Southern Grand Prince, and langjun—each in order presented burial offerings, advancing saddled horses, burial garments, rhinoceros and jade belts, and the like, with memorials listing the quantities.
translations.idiomatic: The Tieli, the Three Fathers' House, the Southern Chancellor, Yaonian Changgun, the Nine Xishou Langjun, Yilibi, the Guoguo Xiangwen, the Ten Zhacha Langjun, the Southern Grand Prince, and the langjun—each in turn presented burial offerings, advancing saddled horses, burial garments, rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, and the like, with memorials itemizing the quantities.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，焚表。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, the memorial was burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, the memorial was burned.

sentences.zh: 諸國所賻器服，親王、諸京留守奠祭、進賻物亦如之。

translations.literal: Funerary goods sent from the various states, and the offerings and tribute presented by princes and frontier commissioners, followed the same practice.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary goods contributed by the various states, and the offerings and tribute presented by princes and frontier commissioners, followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 先帝小斂前一日，皇帝喪服上香，奠酒，哭臨。

translations.literal: On the day before the lesser dressing of the late emperor, the emperor in mourning robes burned incense, offered wine, and mourned at the bier.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before the lesser dressing of the late emperor, the emperor in mourning robes burned incense, offered wine, and mourned at the bier.

sentences.zh: 其夜，北院樞密使、契丹行宮都部署入，小斂。

translations.literal: That night the Northern Chancellor and the Khitan Mobile Court Grand Deployer entered and performed the lesser dressing.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Northern Chancellor and the Khitan Mobile Court Grand Deployer entered and performed the lesser dressing of the corpse.

sentences.zh: 翼日，遣北院樞密副使、林牙，以所赗器服，置之幽宮。

translations.literal: On the following day the Northern Vice Chancellor and the Linya were sent to place the contributed goods and garments in the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day the Northern Vice Chancellor and the Linya were dispatched to place the contributed goods and garments in the inner chamber of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 靈柩升車，親王推之，至食羖之次。

translations.literal: When the spirit coffin was raised onto the carriage, princes pushed it forward to the place of the ram sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit coffin was lifted onto the carriage, princes pushed it forward to the place of the ram sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蓋遼國舊俗，於此刑羖羊以祭。

translations.literal: For by Liao custom a ram was slaughtered here in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: This was an old Liao custom: here a ram was slaughtered as a sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皇族、外戚、諸京州官以次致祭。

translations.literal: The imperial clan, maternal kin, and officials of the various capitals and prefectures offered sacrifice in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan, maternal kin, and officials of the various capitals and prefectures offered sacrifice in succession.

sentences.zh: 至葬所，靈柩降車。

translations.literal: At the burial ground the spirit coffin was lowered from the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial ground the spirit coffin was lowered from the carriage.

sentences.zh: 就舉，皇帝免喪服，步引至長福岡。

translations.literal: For the interment the emperor removed his mourning robes and walked ahead, leading the procession to Changfu Hill.
translations.idiomatic: For the interment the emperor removed his mourning robes and walked ahead on foot, leading the procession to Changfu Hill.

sentences.zh: 是夕，皇帝入陵寢，授遺物於皇族、外戚及諸大臣，乃出。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor entered the tomb chamber, distributed the late emperor's possessions among the imperial clan, maternal kin, and great ministers, and then came out.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the emperor entered the tomb chamber, distributed the late emperor's possessions among the imperial clan, maternal kin, and great ministers, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 命以先帝寢幄，過於陵前神門之木。

translations.literal: He ordered the late emperor's sleeping tent to be carried past the spirit-gate tree before the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the late emperor's sleeping tent to be carried past the spirit-gate tree before the tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝不親往，遣近侍冠服赴之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not go in person but sent close attendants in formal caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not go in person but sent close attendants in formal caps and robes in his stead.

sentences.zh: 初奠，皇帝、皇后率皇族、外戚、使相、節度使、夫人以上命婦皆拜祭，循陵三匝而降。

translations.literal: For the first offering, the emperor and empress led the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, military governors, and titled ladies of third rank and above in bowing and sacrifice; they circled the tomb three times before descending.
translations.idiomatic: For the first offering, the emperor and empress led the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, military governors, and titled ladies of third rank and above in bowing and sacrifice; they circled the tomb three times before descending.

sentences.zh: 再奠，如初。

translations.literal: The second offering followed the first.
translations.idiomatic: The second offering followed the same procedure as the first.

sentences.zh: 辭陵而還。

translations.literal: They took leave of the tomb and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They took leave of the tomb and returned.

sentences.zh: 上謚冊儀：先一日，於菆塗殿西廊設禦幄並臣僚幕次。

translations.literal: Posthumous-title document ceremony: On the preceding day an imperial tent and canopies for officials were set up in the west corridor of the Zangtu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Rite for presenting the posthumous title document: On the preceding day an imperial tent and canopies for the officials were set up in the west corridor of the Zangtu Hall.

sentences.zh: 太樂令展宮懸於殿庭，協律郎設舉麾位。

translations.literal: The Director of Music displayed the palace bells in the court; the pitch-master set the position for raising the baton.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Music hung the palace bells in the courtyard; the pitch-master set the position for raising the conducting baton.

sentences.zh: 至日，北南面臣僚朝服，昧爽赴菆塗殿。

translations.literal: On the day, officials of north and south in court dress came at dawn to the Zangtu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, officials of the northern and southern administrations, in court dress, arrived at dawn at the Zangtu Hall.

sentences.zh: 先置冊、寶案於西廊下。

translations.literal: The cases for the document and seal were first placed below the west corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The cases for the document and seal were first set out beneath the west corridor.

sentences.zh: 閣使引皇帝至禦幄，服寬衣皂帶。

translations.literal: The gate attendant led the emperor to the imperial tent to don wide mourning robes with a black belt.
translations.idiomatic: The gate attendant led the emperor to the imperial tent to don wide mourning robes with a black belt.

sentences.zh: 臣僚班齊，分班引入，響殿合班立定。

translations.literal: When the officials' ranks were complete, they were led in by groups, entered the hall, and took their stands in formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials' ranks were complete, they were led in by groups, entered the hall at the signal, and took their places in formation.

sentences.zh: 引冊案上殿至褥位，寶案次之，設於西階。

translations.literal: The document case was brought up to the hall to the cushion position, the seal case next; both were set on the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: The document case was brought up to the hall to the cushion position, with the seal case following; both were set on the west steps.

sentences.zh: 閣使引皇帝自西階升殿。

translations.literal: The gate attendant led the emperor up the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: The gate attendant led the emperor up the west steps.

sentences.zh: 初行，樂作；

translations.literal: When he first set out, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: As he first set out, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 至位立，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reached his place and stood, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when he reached his place and stood, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使揖皇帝鞠躬再拜，陪位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Commissioner motioned the emperor to bow twice; those in attendance also bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Commissioner motioned the emperor to bow twice; all those in attendance bowed twice as well.

sentences.zh: 翰林使執臺盞以進，皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Commissioner advanced holding the offering tray; the emperor bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Commissioner advanced bearing the offering tray; the emperor bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 引皇至神座前，跪奠三，樂作，進奠訖，復位，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor was led before the spirit seat, knelt, and presented offerings three times; music sounded; when the offerings were complete he returned to his place and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was led before the spirit seat, knelt, and presented offerings three times; music sounded; when the offerings were finished he returned to his place and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 又再拜，陪位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: He bowed twice again; those in attendance did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice again, and all those in attendance did the same.

sentences.zh: 引帝於神座前。

translations.literal: The emperor was led before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was led before the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 北面立。

translations.literal: He stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: He stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 捧冊函者去蓋，進前跪。

translations.literal: One bearing the document casket removed the cover and advanced, kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: The bearer of the document casket removed the cover and advanced, kneeling.

sentences.zh: 冊案退，置殿西壁下。

translations.literal: The document case withdrew and was placed beneath the west wall of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The document case was withdrawn and set beneath the west wall of the hall.

sentences.zh: 引讀冊者進前，俯伏跪，自通全銜臣讀謚冊。

translations.literal: The reader of the document advanced, prostrated himself, and read the posthumous-title document, beginning with his full official title.
translations.idiomatic: The reader of the document advanced, prostrated himself, announced his full official title, and read the posthumous-title document.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，俯伏興，復位。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished he rose from prostration and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished he rose from prostration and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 捧冊函者置於案上，捧寶函者進前跪，讀寶官通銜跪讀訖，引皇帝至褥位再拜，陪位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: One bearing the document casket set it on the case; one bearing the seal casket advanced and knelt; the seal reader with full title knelt and read; then the emperor was led to the cushion and bowed twice, and those in attendance did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The bearer of the document casket set it on the case; the bearer of the seal casket advanced and knelt; the seal reader announced his full title, knelt, and read; then the emperor was led to the cushion and bowed twice, and all those in attendance did the same.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，引皇帝歸禦幄。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete the emperor was led back to the imperial tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the emperor was led back to the imperial tent.

sentences.zh: 初行，樂作；

translations.literal: When he first set out, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: As he set out, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 至禦幄，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reached the imperial tent, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when he reached the imperial tent, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 引臣僚分班出。

translations.literal: The officials were led out by groups.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were led out in groups.

sentences.zh: 若皇太后奠酒，依常儀。

translations.literal: If the Empress Dowager presented wine, the usual procedure was followed.
translations.idiomatic: If the Empress Dowager presented wine, the usual procedure was followed.

sentences.zh: 忌辰儀：先一日，奏忌辰榜子，預寫名紙。

translations.literal: Anniversary-of-death rite: On the preceding day a memorial of the anniversary was submitted and name slips were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Anniversary-of-death rite: On the preceding day a memorial announcing the anniversary was submitted and name slips were prepared in advance.

sentences.zh: 大紙一幅，用陰面後第三行書「文武百僚宰臣某以下謹詣西上閣門進名奉慰」。

translations.literal: On one large sheet, in the third line from the back on the yin side, was written: "The civil and military officials, ministers, and all below, in reverence proceed to the Western Upper Gate to present their names in condolence."
translations.idiomatic: On one large sheet, in the third line from the back on the yin side, was written: "The civil and military officials, ministers, and all below, in reverence proceed to the Western Upper Gate to present their names in condolence."

sentences.zh: 至日，應拜大小臣僚並皂衣、皂鞓帶，四鼓至時，於幕次前，在京於僧寺，班齊，依位望闕敘立。

translations.literal: On the day, all officials great and small who were to bow wore black robes and black girdles; at the fourth watch they assembled before the canopies—in the capital, at a Buddhist temple—formed their ranks by position, and faced the palace gate in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, all officials great and small who were to bow wore black robes and black girdles. At the fourth watch they assembled before the canopies—in the capital, at a Buddhist temple—formed their ranks by position, and stood in order facing the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 直日舍人跪右，執名紙在前，班首以下皆再拜。

translations.literal: The duty secretary knelt to the right, holding the name sheet in front; from the head of the rank down all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The duty secretary knelt to the right, holding the name sheet before him; from the head of the rank downward all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 引退。

translations.literal: They withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew.

sentences.zh: 名紙於宣徽使面付內侍奏聞。

translations.literal: The name sheet was handed to the inner attendant before the Palace Commissioner, who reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The name sheet was handed to the inner attendant in the presence of the Palace Commissioner, who reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宋使祭奠吊慰儀：太皇太后至菆塗殿，服喪服。

translations.literal: Song envoy condolence and consolation rite: The Grand Empress Dowager came to the Zangtu Hall in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Song envoys presenting condolences and comfort: The Grand Empress Dowager came to the Zangtu Hall dressed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 太后於北間南面垂簾坐，皇帝於南間北面坐，使至幕次。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sat behind a curtain on the south side of the north chamber; the emperor sat on the north side of the south chamber facing north; the envoys arrived at the side tents.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sat behind a curtain on the south side of the north chamber; the emperor sat on the north side of the south chamber facing north; the envoys arrived at the side tents.

sentences.zh: 宣賜素服、皂帶，更衣訖，引南北臣僚入班，立定。

translations.literal: They were granted plain mourning dress and a black belt; when they had changed, officials of north and south were led in and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted plain mourning dress and a black belt; when they had changed, officials of the northern and southern administrations were led in and took their places.

sentences.zh: 可矮墩以下，並上殿依位立。

translations.literal: Those from the Aidian rank down all ascended the hall and stood by position.
translations.idiomatic: Those of Aidian rank and below all ascended the hall and stood in their assigned places.

sentences.zh: 先引祭奠使副捧祭文南洞門入，殿上下臣僚並舉哀，至丹墀立定。

translations.literal: The condolence envoys were first led in through the south gate carrying the elegy; officials above and below the hall all wailed; they halted on the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence envoys were first led in through the south gate bearing the elegy; officials above and below the hall all wailed; they halted on the red steps of the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 西上閣門使自南階下，受祭文，上殿啟封，置於香案。

translations.literal: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the south steps, received the elegy, ascended, opened the seal, and placed it on the incense table.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the south steps, received the elegy, ascended the hall, broke the seal, and placed it on the incense table.

sentences.zh: 哭止，祭奠禮物列殿前。

translations.literal: Wailing ceased and condolence gifts were arrayed before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing ceased, and the condolence gifts were arrayed before the hall.

sentences.zh: 引使副南階上殿，至褥位立，揖，再拜。

translations.literal: The envoys were led up the south steps to the cushion and stood; they bowed with a motion and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were led up the south steps to the cushion and stood; they bowed with a gesture and then bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 引太使近前上香，退，再拜。

translations.literal: The chief envoy advanced to burn incense and withdrew, then bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy was led forward to burn incense, withdrew, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 大使近前跪，捧臺盞，進奠酒三，教坊奏樂，退，再拜，揖，中書二舍人跪捧祭文，引大使近前俯伏跪，讀訖，舉哀。

translations.literal: The chief envoy advanced, knelt, and held the offering tray; he presented wine three times while the Music Office played; he withdrew, bowed twice, bowed with a motion; two Zhongshu secretaries knelt holding the elegy; the chief envoy was led forward, prostrated himself, read it, and wailing rose.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy advanced, knelt, and held the offering tray; he presented wine three times while the Music Office played. He withdrew, bowed twice, and bowed with a gesture. Two Zhongshu secretaries knelt bearing the elegy; the chief envoy was led forward, prostrated himself, read it to the end, and wailing rose.

sentences.zh: 引使副下殿立定，哭止。

translations.literal: The envoys were led down and stood below; wailing ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were led down from the hall and stood below; wailing ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮物擔床出畢，引使副近南，面北立。

translations.literal: When the gift litters had all been brought out, the envoys were led southward to stand facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When the gift litters had all been brought out, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.

sentences.zh: 勾吊慰使副南洞門入。

translations.literal: The consolation envoys were summoned to enter through the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: The consolation envoys were summoned to enter through the south gate.

sentences.zh: 四使同見大行皇帝靈，再拜。

translations.literal: All four envoys together viewed the spirit of the late emperor and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: All four envoys together viewed the spirit of the late emperor and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 引出，歸幕次。

translations.literal: They were led out and returned to the side tents.
translations.idiomatic: They were led out and returned to the side tents.

sentences.zh: 皇太后別殿坐，服喪服。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sat in a separate hall in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sat in a separate hall dressed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 先引北南面臣僚並於殿上下依位立，吊慰使副捧書匣右入，當殿立。

translations.literal: Officials of the north and south were first led to stand above and below the hall by position; the consolation envoys entered carrying the letter casket on the right and stood before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the northern and southern administrations were first led to stand above and below the hall in their places; the consolation envoys entered carrying the letter casket on the right and stood before the hall.

sentences.zh: 閤門使右下殿受書匣，上殿奏「封全」。

translations.literal: The Gate Attendant came down on the right, received the casket, ascended, and reported "the seal is intact."
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Attendant came down on the right, received the casket, ascended the hall, and reported, "The seal is intact."

sentences.zh: 開讀訖，引使副南階上殿，傳達吊慰訖，退，下殿立。

translations.literal: When it was opened and read, the envoys were led up the south steps, conveyed their condolences, withdrew, and stood below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When it was opened and read, the envoys were led up the south steps, conveyed their condolences, withdrew, and stood below the hall.

sentences.zh: 引禮物擔床過畢，引使副近南，北面立。

translations.literal: When the gift litters had passed, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When the gift litters had passed, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.

sentences.zh: 勾祭奠使副入。

translations.literal: The condolence envoys were summoned to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence envoys were summoned to enter.

sentences.zh: 四使同見。

translations.literal: All four envoys were received together.
translations.idiomatic: All four envoys were received together.

sentences.zh: 鞠躬，再拜。

translations.literal: They bowed with a motion and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed with a gesture and then bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜。

translations.literal: Without leaving the formation they reported "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings" and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving formation they reported, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 出班，謝面天顏，又再拜，立定。

translations.literal: They left the formation, thanked him for appearing in person, bowed twice again, and stood.
translations.idiomatic: They left formation, thanked him for appearing in person, bowed twice again, and stood at attention.

sentences.zh: 宣徽傳聖旨撫問，就位謝，再拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Commissioner conveyed the imperial message of comfort; they took their places and thanked him, bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Commissioner conveyed the imperial message of comfort; they took their places and offered thanks, bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 引出，歸幕次。

translations.literal: They were led out and returned to the side tents.
translations.idiomatic: They were led out and returned to the side tents.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御南殿，服喪服。

translations.literal: The emperor presided in the southern hall in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor presided in the southern hall dressed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 使副入見，如見皇太后儀，加謝遠接撫問、湯藥，再拜。

translations.literal: The envoys entered for an audience by the same procedure as for the Empress Dowager, with additional thanks for escort on the journey, comfort, and medicine, bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys entered for an audience following the same procedure as for the Empress Dowager, with additional thanks for the escort on their journey, expressions of comfort, and provisions of medicine, bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 次宣賜使副並從人，祭奠使副別賜讀祭文例物。

translations.literal: Next gifts were bestowed on the envoys and their attendants; the condolence envoys separately received the customary items for reading the elegy.
translations.idiomatic: Next, gifts were bestowed on the envoys and their attendants; the condolence envoys separately received the customary items granted for reading the elegy.

sentences.zh: 即日就館賜宴。

translations.literal: That same day a banquet was given at their lodging.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a banquet was given for them at their lodging.

sentences.zh: 高麗、夏國奉吊、進賻等使禮，略如之。

translations.literal: The rites of Goryeo and Western Xia envoys presenting condolences and tribute were much the same.
translations.idiomatic: The rites for envoys from Goryeo and Western Xia presenting condolences and tribute were much the same.

sentences.zh: 道宗崩，天祚皇帝問禮於耶律固。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daozong died, Emperor Tianzuo asked Ye Lü Gu about the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daozong died, Emperor Tianzuo consulted Ye Lü Gu about the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 宋國遣使吊及致祭、歸赗，皇帝喪服，禦遊仙之北別殿。

translations.literal: The Song state sent envoys to offer condolences, present sacrifices, and return funerary gifts; the emperor in mourning robes presided in the separate hall north of Youxian.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court dispatched envoys to offer condolences, present sacrifices, and return funerary gifts; the emperor, dressed in mourning, presided in the separate hall north of the Youxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 使入門，皇帝哭。

translations.literal: When the envoys entered the gate, the emperor wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys entered, the emperor wept.

sentences.zh: 使者詣柩前上香，讀祭文訖，又哭。

translations.literal: The envoys went before the bier to burn incense; when the elegy had been read, they wept again.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys went before the bier to burn incense; when the elegy had been read, they wept again.

sentences.zh: 有司讀遺詔，慟哭。

translations.literal: The proper offices read the testament; there was bitter wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices read the late emperor's testament, and bitter wailing broke out.

sentences.zh: 使者出，少頃，復入，陳賻赗於柩前，皇帝入臨哭。

translations.literal: The envoys withdrew; after a short while they entered again and displayed funerary gifts before the bier; the emperor came in to mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys withdrew; after a short while they entered again and presented funerary gifts before the bier; the emperor came in person to mourn and weep.

sentences.zh: 退，更衣禦遊仙殿南之幄殿。

translations.literal: He withdrew, changed his garments, and presided in the tent hall south of the Youxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew, changed his garments, and took his seat in the tent hall south of the Youxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 使者入見且辭，敕有司賜宴於館。

translations.literal: The envoys entered for an audience and took their leave; he ordered the proper offices to grant a banquet at their lodging.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys entered for an audience and took their leave; he ordered the responsible offices to grant them a banquet at their lodging.

sentences.zh: 宋使告哀儀：皇帝素冠服，臣僚皂袍、皂鞓帶。

translations.literal: Song envoy announcement-of-mourning rite: The emperor wore plain cap and robes; officials wore black robes and black girdles.
translations.idiomatic: Rite for Song envoys announcing mourning: The emperor wore a plain cap and robes; the officials wore black robes and black girdles.

sentences.zh: 宋使奉書右入。

translations.literal: The Song envoys entered on the right bearing the letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoys entered on the right, bearing the letter.

sentences.zh: 丹墀內立。

translations.literal: They stood within the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: They stood within the red steps of the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 西上閣門使右階下殿，受書匣：上殿，欄內鞠躬，奏「封全」。

translations.literal: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the right steps, received the letter casket, ascended, bowed within the railing, and reported "the seal is intact."
translations.idiomatic: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the right steps, received the letter casket, ascended the hall, bowed within the railing, and reported, "The seal is intact."

sentences.zh: 開封，於殿西案授宰相讀訖，皇帝舉哀。

translations.literal: The seal was broken; at the western table of the hall it was handed to the chief minister to read; when the reading was finished, the emperor raised a lament.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was broken; at the western table of the hall it was handed to the chief minister to read; when the reading was finished, the emperor broke into lamentation.

sentences.zh: 舍人引使者右階上，欄內俯跪，附奏起居訖，俯興，立。

translations.literal: The secretary led the envoys up the right steps; within the railing they prostrated themselves, presented a memorial on the emperor's health, rose from prostration, and stood.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary led the envoys up the right steps; within the railing they prostrated themselves, presented a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health, rose, and stood.

sentences.zh: 皇帝宣問「南朝皇帝聖躬萬福」，使者跪奏「來時皇帝聖躬萬福」起，退。

translations.literal: The emperor announced the inquiry "May the emperor of the Southern Court enjoy ten thousand blessings"; the envoys knelt and reported "When we departed, the emperor enjoyed ten thousand blessings," then rose and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired, "May the emperor of the Southern Court enjoy ten thousand blessings"; the envoys knelt and reported, "When we departed, the emperor enjoyed ten thousand blessings," then rose and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 舍人引使者右階下殿，於丹墀西，面東鞠躬。

translations.literal: The secretary led the envoys down the right steps; on the west of the red steps they faced east and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary led the envoys down the right steps; on the west side of the courtyard they faced east and bowed.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人通使者名某祗候見，再拜。

translations.literal: The interpreter secretary announced the envoy's name and that he was in attendance to be received; they bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreter secretary announced the envoy's name and that he was in attendance to be received; they bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜。

translations.literal: Without leaving the formation they reported "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings" and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving formation they reported, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 出班，謝面天顏，再拜。

translations.literal: They left the formation, thanked him for appearing in person, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They left formation, thanked him for appearing in person, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 又出班，謝遠接、撫問、湯藥，再拜。

translations.literal: They left the formation again, thanked him for the escort on the journey, comfort, and medicine, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They left formation again and thanked him for the escort on their journey, expressions of comfort, and provisions of medicine, bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 贊祗候，引出，就幕次，宣賜衣物。

translations.literal: They were announced in attendance, led out, and went to the side tents; garments were bestowed by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: They were announced in attendance, led out to the side tents, and garments were bestowed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 引從人入，通名拜，奏「聖躬萬福」，出就幕，賜衣，如使者之儀。

translations.literal: Their attendants were led in; names were announced and they bowed, reporting "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings"; they went out to the tents and were granted clothing by the same procedure as the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants were led in; names were announced and they bowed, reporting, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings"; they went out to the tents and were granted clothing following the same procedure as the envoys.

sentences.zh: 又引使者入，面殿鞠躬，贊謝恩。

translations.literal: The envoys were led in again; facing the hall they bowed, and thanks for imperial favor were announced.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were led in again; facing the hall they bowed, and thanks for imperial favor were announced.

sentences.zh: 再贊「有敕賜宴」，再拜。

translations.literal: It was announced again "By imperial order a banquet is granted"; they bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: It was announced again, "By imperial order a banquet is granted"; they bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊祗候，出就幕次宴。

translations.literal: They were announced in attendance and went out to the side tents for the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: They were announced in attendance and went out to the side tents for the banquet.

sentences.zh: 引從人謝恩，拜敕賜宴，皆如初。

translations.literal: Their attendants were led in to thank him for imperial favor and bow for the granted banquet, all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants were led in to offer thanks for imperial favor and bow for the granted banquet, all following the same procedure as before.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，歸館。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished, they returned to their lodging.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet was finished, they returned to their lodging.

sentences.zh: 宋使進遺留禮物儀：百官昧爽朝服，殿前班立。

translations.literal: Song envoy presentation of bequeathed gifts rite: At dawn all officials in court dress formed their ranks before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Rite for Song envoys presenting bequeathed gifts: At dawn all officials in court dress formed their ranks before the hall.

sentences.zh: 宋遺留使、告登位使副入內門，館伴副使引謝登位使就幕次坐。

translations.literal: The Song bequest envoys and the announcement-of-accession envoys entered the inner gate; the host deputy led the accession-thanks envoys to be seated at the side tents.
translations.idiomatic: The Song bequest envoys and the announcement-of-accession envoys entered the inner gate; the host deputy led the accession-thanks envoys to be seated at the side tents.

sentences.zh: 館伴大使與遺留使副奉書入，至西上閣門外氈位立。

translations.literal: The host chief envoy and the bequest envoys entered bearing the letter and stood at the felt mat position outside the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The host chief envoy and the bequest envoys entered bearing the letter and stood at the felt mat position outside the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 閣使受書匣，置殿西階下案。

translations.literal: The gate attendant received the letter casket and placed it on the table below the west steps of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The gate attendant received the letter casket and placed it on the table below the west steps of the hall.

sentences.zh: 引進使引遺留物於西上閣門入，即於廊下橫門出。

translations.literal: The usher led the bequeathed goods in through the Western Upper Gate and immediately out through the transverse gate beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The usher led the bequeathed goods in through the Western Upper Gate and immediately out through the transverse gate beneath the corridor.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升殿坐。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the hall and took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the hall and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使押殿前班起居畢，引宰臣押文武班起居，引中書令西階上殿，奏宋使見榜子。

translations.literal: When the Palace Commissioner had led the hall-front ranks in salutation, he led the chief ministers to lead the civil and military ranks in salutation, then led the Director of the Secretariat up the west steps to report the Song envoys' arrival memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Palace Commissioner had led the hall-front ranks in salutation, he led the chief ministers to lead the civil and military ranks in salutation, then led the Director of the Secretariat up the west steps to report the Song envoys' arrival memorial.

sentences.zh: 契丹臣僚起居，控鶴官起居。

translations.literal: Khitan officials saluted; Crane-Control officers saluted.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan officials saluted; the Crane-Control officers saluted.

sentences.zh: 遺留使副西上閣門入，面殿立。

translations.literal: The bequest envoys entered through the Western Upper Gate and stood facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The bequest envoys entered through the Western Upper Gate and stood facing the hall.

sentences.zh: 舍人引使副西階上殿，附奏起居訖，引西階下殿，於丹墀東，西面鞠躬，通名奏「聖躬萬福」，如告哀使之儀。

translations.literal: The secretary led the envoys up the west steps, presented a memorial on the emperor's health, led them down the west steps, and on the east of the red steps they faced west, bowed, announced their names, and reported "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," as in the announcement-of-mourning envoy rite.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary led the envoys up the west steps, presented a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health, led them down the west steps, and on the east side of the courtyard they faced west, bowed, announced their names, and reported, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," following the same procedure as the announcement-of-mourning envoys.

sentences.zh: 謝面天顏，謝遠接、撫問、湯藥。

translations.literal: They thanked him for appearing in person and for the escort on the journey, comfort, and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: They thanked him for appearing in person and for the escort on their journey, expressions of comfort, and provisions of medicine.

sentences.zh: 引遺留使從人見亦如之。

translations.literal: The bequest envoys' attendants were led in for an audience in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: The bequest envoys' attendants were led in for an audience in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 次引告登位使副奉書匣，於東上閣門入，面殿立。

translations.literal: Next the announcement-of-accession envoys were led in bearing the letter casket through the Eastern Upper Gate and stood facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Next the announcement-of-accession envoys were led in bearing the letter casket through the Eastern Upper Gate and stood facing the hall.

sentences.zh: 閣使東階下殿，受書匣。

translations.literal: The gate attendant came down the east steps and received the letter casket.
translations.idiomatic: The gate attendant came down the east steps and received the letter casket.

sentences.zh: 中書令讀訖，舍人引使副東階上殿，附奏起居。

translations.literal: When the Director of the Secretariat had finished reading, the secretary led the envoys up the east steps and presented a memorial on the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: When the Director of the Secretariat had finished reading, the secretary led the envoys up the east steps and presented a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 引下殿，南面立。

translations.literal: They were led down from the hall and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: They were led down from the hall and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 告登位禮物入，即於廊下橫門出。

translations.literal: The accession-announcement gifts entered and immediately went out through the transverse gate beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The accession-announcement gifts were brought in and immediately taken out through the transverse gate beneath the corridor.

sentences.zh: 退，西面鞠躬，附奏起居，謝面天顏、遠接等，皆如遺留使之儀。

translations.literal: They withdrew, faced west and bowed, presented a memorial on the emperor's health, and thanked him for appearing in person and for the escort on the journey, all as in the bequest envoy rite.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew, faced west and bowed, presented a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health, and thanked him for appearing in person and for the escort on their journey, all following the same procedure as the bequest envoys.

sentences.zh: 宣賜遺留、登位兩使副並從人衣物，如告哀使。

translations.literal: Garments were bestowed by imperial order on the bequest and accession envoys and their attendants, as for the announcement-of-mourning envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Garments were bestowed by imperial order on the bequest and accession envoys and their attendants, as for the announcement-of-mourning envoys.

sentences.zh: 應坐臣僚皆上殿就位立，分引兩使副等於兩廊立。

translations.literal: All officials who were to be seated ascended the hall and took their places; the two groups of envoys were led separately to stand in the two corridors.
translations.idiomatic: All officials who were to be seated ascended the hall and took their places; the two groups of envoys were led separately to stand in the two corridors.

sentences.zh: 皇帝問使副「沖涉不易」丹墀內五拜。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired of the envoys "Your journey through ice and snow was not easy"; within the red steps they bowed five times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired of the envoys, "Your journey through ice and snow was not easy"; within the courtyard they bowed five times.

sentences.zh: 各引上殿祗候位立。

translations.literal: Each group was led up to the hall to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Each group was led up to the hall to stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 大臣進灑，皇帝飲酒。

translations.literal: A great minister advanced the libation; the emperor drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: A great minister advanced the libation; the emperor drank wine.

sentences.zh: 契丹通，漢人贊，殿上臣僚皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: The Khitan announcer called; the Chinese master of ceremonies led; all officials on the hall bowed and cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan announcer called; the Chinese master of ceremonies led; all officials on the hall bowed and cried, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐，行酒肴、茶膳、饅頭畢，從人出水飯畢，臣僚皆起。

translations.literal: They were led to their seats; when wine, dishes, tea, food, and steamed buns had been served, and when the attendants had been given rice and soup, all officials rose.
translations.idiomatic: They were led to their seats; when wine, dishes, tea, food, and steamed buns had been served, and when the attendants had been given rice and soup, all officials rose.

sentences.zh: 契丹通，漢人贊，皆再拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: The Khitan announcer called; the Chinese master of ceremonies led; all bowed twice and cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan announcer called; the Chinese master of ceremonies led; all bowed twice and cried, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 各祗候。

translations.literal: Each stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Each stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 獨引宋使副下殿謝，五拜。

translations.literal: The Song envoys alone were led down from the hall to offer thanks, bowing five times.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoys alone were led down from the hall to offer thanks, bowing five times.

sentences.zh: 引出。

translations.literal: They were led out.
translations.idiomatic: They were led out.

sentences.zh: 控鶴官門外祗候，報閣門無事供奉官卷班出。

translations.literal: Crane-Control officers waited outside the gate; it was reported that the gate was clear of business and the palace attendants filed out in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Crane-Control officers waited outside the gate; it was reported that the gate was clear of business and the palace attendants filed out in ranks.

sentences.zh: 高麗、夏國告終儀：先期，於先宮左右下禦帳，設使客幕次於東南。

translations.literal: Goryeo and Western Xia announcement-of-death rite: In advance, below the imperial tents to left and right of the former palace, guest tents for envoys were set up in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Rite for Goryeo and Western Xia envoys announcing a ruler's death: In advance, below the imperial tents to the left and right of the former palace, guest tents for the envoys were set up in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 至日，北面臣僚各常服，其餘臣僚並朝服，入朝。

translations.literal: On the day, northern officials each wore ordinary dress; the remaining officials all wore court dress and entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, northern officials each wore ordinary dress; the remaining officials all wore court dress and entered court.

sentences.zh: 使者至幕次，有司以嗣子表狀先呈樞密院，準備奏呈。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached the tents, the proper offices first presented the heir's memorial to the Privy Council, preparing it for presentation to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached the tents, the responsible offices first presented the heir's memorial to the Privy Council, preparing it for presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先引北面臣僚並矮墩已上近禦帳，相對立，其餘臣僚依班位序立。

translations.literal: Northern officials and those of Aidian rank and above were first led near the imperial tents to stand facing one another; the remaining officials stood in order by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Northern officials and those of Aidian rank and above were first led near the imperial tents to stand facing one another; the remaining officials stood in order by rank.

sentences.zh: 引告終人使右入，至丹墀，面殿立。

translations.literal: The announcement-of-death envoys were led in on the right to the red steps and stood facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The announcement-of-death envoys were led in on the right to the courtyard and stood facing the hall.

sentences.zh: 引右上，立；

translations.literal: They were led up on the right and stood;
translations.idiomatic: They were led up on the right and stood;

sentences.zh: 揖少前，拜，跪奏訖，宣問。

translations.literal: bowed with a motion and advanced slightly, bowed, knelt and presented their memorial; the imperial inquiry was announced.
translations.idiomatic: bowed with a gesture and advanced slightly, bowed, knelt and presented their memorial; the imperial inquiry was announced.

sentences.zh: 若嗣子已立，恭身受聖旨。

translations.literal: If the heir had already been established, he respectfully received the imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: If the heir had already been established, he respectfully received the imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 奏訖，復位。

translations.literal: When the presentation was finished, they returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation was finished, they returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 嗣子未立。

translations.literal: If the heir had not yet been established,
translations.idiomatic: If the heir had not yet been established,

sentences.zh: 不宣問，引右下丹墀，面北鞠躬。

translations.literal: the inquiry was not announced; they were led down on the right to the red steps and bowed facing north.
translations.idiomatic: the inquiry was not announced; they were led down on the right to the courtyard and bowed facing north.

sentences.zh: 通班畢，引面殿再拜。

translations.literal: When the ranks had been announced, they were led to face the hall and bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks had been announced, they were led to face the hall and bow twice.

sentences.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜。

translations.literal: Without leaving the formation they reported "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings" and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving formation they reported, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 出班，謝面天顏，復位，再拜。

translations.literal: They left the formation, thanked him for appearing in person, returned to their places, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They left formation, thanked him for appearing in person, returned to their places, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 出班，謝遠接，復位，再拜。

translations.literal: They left the formation, thanked him for the escort on the journey, returned to their places, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: They left formation, thanked him for the escort on their journey, returned to their places, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊祗候，退就幕次。

translations.literal: They were announced in attendance and withdrew to the side tents.
translations.idiomatic: They were announced in attendance and withdrew to the side tents.

sentences.zh: 再入，依前面北鞠躬，通辭，再拜；

translations.literal: They entered again, bowed facing north as before, announced their farewell, and bowed twice;
translations.idiomatic: They entered again, bowed facing north as before, announced their farewell, and bowed twice;

sentences.zh: 敘戀闕，再拜。

translations.literal: expressed their longing for the court and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: expressed their longing for the court and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊「好去」。

translations.literal: "Farewell" was announced.
translations.idiomatic: "Farewell" was announced.

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was complete.
